Hi Elena,

Thanks again for taking the demo this morning — appreciate you and Rajiv carving out time. Per our call, I wanted to capture the concrete next steps and a short technical checklist so we can scope the Dedicated capacity POC cleanly.

Quick summary of what we discussed:
- Integration surface: SDK + REST for chat/generation and separate embeddings endpoint for search/reranking.
- Auth options: API tokens for initial POC; interest in KMS-backed keys and mTLS for production.
- Routing & fallbacks: primary region US-West, fallback to Redwood-hosted variant for outages.
- Throughput needs: you mentioned baseline 20 qps for inference, spikes to ~80 qps during batch jobs; typical response ~400 tokens.
- SLO priorities: 95th pct latency under 300ms for short completions; embeddings can be async.

Proposed immediate next steps (we're ready to start once we have your answers to the short items below):
1) Tech answers / attach security questionnaire (Rajiv)
2) Provide sample API pattern (Dev) + quick SDK bootstrap guide (Avery)
3) POC sizing proposal for Dedicated pool + queue design (Maya)
4) Follow-up call to lock scope (30 min) — proposed Thu 11/07 10:00 PT

Please see the attached "redwood-integration-checklist.xlsx" — it's a short table where you can drop in expected steady-state QPS, peak QPS, and retention/security requirements.

I'll hold a tentative follow-up for Thu; happy to move if that doesn't work.

Best,
Jonas
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Hi Elena / Rajiv — thanks for the quick turnaround. A couple of technical notes that should help while you complete the questionnaire: 

1) SDK + Auth options (quick):
   - Offer native SDKs (Python/Go/Node) that take either bearer token or mTLS certs.
   - For rotation, Redwood supports short-lived tokens with KMS integration (customer-managed keys) and a key-rotation webhook that can be polled by your credential manager.
   - For POC, we can provide a service account token with adjustable TTL.

2) Routing and structured output / tool calling: 
   - Tool calling: SDK supports structured tool call responses (JSON schema) and native helpers to validate output and route to your downstream services.
   - Routing: we can pin requests to a private Dedicated pool in US-West and set fallback policy to the hosted model if capacity is exhausted.

3) Embeddings & reranker notes: 
   - We recommend sending shorter context for embedding calls and batching where possible; our embeddings endpoint supports batch sizes up to 64 vectors per request, and we can enable async jobs for large backfills.
   - Reranking strategy: generate top-K candidates (K=20) via dense retrieval then run a lightweight llama reranker in the Dedicated pool for quality-sensitive paths.

I'll drop an SDK bootstrap gist in the shared Drive and a minimal curl example you can use for a smoke test.

Quick ask for sizing: can you share expected mean tokens per request and any peak burst window (e.g., bursts lasting >1 minute vs ~5s)? That will determine queue depth vs concurrency tradeoffs.

Thanks,
Dev
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Dev / team — attaching a short note from our SRE side: 

- Baseline: 18 qps steady for low-latency fraud checks.
- Peak: 75 qps for end-of-day processing windows (peaks last ~8-12 minutes).
- Mean response tokens: ~420 tokens for generation; embeddings responses ~384 dims returned as 1536-d vectors.
- Security: KMS-managed keys are required for production; we'll need mTLS on the Dedicated control plane.

We filled the checklist and dropped it in the Drive link Jonas shared. For the POC we prefer a conservative concurrency limit per GPU (we currently budget ~6 concurrent generation calls per GPU to meet 300ms p95). If you can provide a queueing model that guarantees our p95 targets under burst loads that would be ideal.

Rajiv
SRE Lead | Ledgerly
From: Maya Srinivasan <maya.srinivasan@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Post-demo: Ledgerly - SDK/Auth/Throughput checklist & next steps

Thanks Rajiv — good details. I've sketched a POC Sizing + Queue recommendation and attached the diagram (arch-proposal-queue-model.png). High-level proposal: 

- Dedicated pool: 4 x A40-class GPUs (start), autoscale +1 node at 80% sustained CPU/GPU utilization.
- Concurrency per GPU: cap 6 concurrent generation calls (matches your target). Queue depth: 300 requests with dynamic priority lanes (critical fraud checks hop the queue).
- Batching: enable dynamic batching for non-critical paths to increase throughput; keep fraud checks on single-token latency path.
- Fallback policy: if queue length > 250, spill to hosted read-only model for non-sensitive requests.
- Monitoring: per-route latency SLOs with alerting at 95th pct and token-based billing report.

Immediate asks for us to finalize sizing:
1) Confirm whether the 75 qps peak is cumulative across all customers or per-region (assumed per-region).
2) Acceptable maximum cold-start delay for burst scaling (we typically size for < 60s cold-start).
3) Any constraints on allowing fallback to hosted variant for lower-sensitivity workloads.

If that looks reasonable I'll prepare an updated capacity quote and a 2-week POC plan.

-- Maya
Customer Success Manager (Infra) | Redwood Inference

Thanks all — the recommendations look good. Quick answers:

- Peak 75 qps is per-region.
- Cold-start tolerance: up to 45s acceptable for background/backfill jobs; fraud-critical flows require warm capacity (no cold-start).
- Fallback to hosted variant: acceptable for non-sensitive analytical workloads but not for PII/fraud-critical paths.

Please go ahead and produce the 2-week POC plan and capacity quote. We can confirm the Thu 11/07 10am PT call — Rajiv and I will be on. Also please include a short note on contract terms (trial credits / short-term SLA) so procurement can review.

Elena
